_provenance.source: DUKES Table 5.7.A 'Capacity by fuel, MW', worksheet '5.7', rows for 'All generating companies' -- Coal fired / Gas fired / Nuclear stations
_provenance.units: MW, de-rated/nameplate transmission-connected + embedded plant capacity at calendar year end, ALL GENERATING COMPANIES (major power producers + other generators combined)
_provenance.measurement_basis: DESNZ's own plant-capacity register (licensed/connected generating plant by fuel type) -- a DIFFERENT DESNZ table from w1_7_dukes_installed_capacity_annual.json (that one is DUKES/Energy Trends Table ET 6.1, renewables-only, Ofgem RO/FiT/REGO accreditation basis). Independent of the Elexon AGWS settlement feed sim/weather_price_chain.py ingests (anti-marking-own-homework).
_provenance.technology_basis: 'Gas fired' = CCGT + OCGT/gas-turbine capacity summed (verified: Table 5.7.B's separately-reported CCGT + gas-turbine rows sum exactly to Table 5.7.A's 'Gas fired' row, e.g. 2016 major-power-producer CCGT 29706 + gas turbines 864.5 = 30570.5 = the 5.7.A MPP gas-fired figure). 'Coal fired' = conventional coal steam stations. 'Nuclear stations' = all nuclear capacity. DISPATCHABLE_CAPACITY_MW in sim/price_engine.py sums these three (coal+gas+nuclear) -- the same CCGT/OCGT/coal/nuclear basket the module's own pre-existing R10 docstring named for its flat 35000 MW constant, now time-varying. Interconnector import capacity (also named in that docstring) remains OUT of this series -- DUKES 5.13 is a further, un-fetched table; a disclosed, unchanged gap (the original flat constant never included it either).
